Under what conditions can quantum fields and gravitational functional integrals accommodate spacetime topology changes and their associated singularities?

How does the Hilbert-space inequality Tr(BC) ≤ Tr(B)Tr(C) for positive operators arise from semiclassical gravitational path integrals, including topology sums, quantum corrections and perturbative higher-derivative terms?

How can a background-independent Lorentzian gravitational path integral be regularized nonperturbatively, evaluated numerically, and used to extract invariant quantum-geometric observables and a candidate continuum theory?
Can gravitational dynamics suppress virtual black-hole configurations in a Lorentzian path integral, thereby opening a possible loophole in black-hole arguments against global symmetries?

How prevalent are light-conical singularities in Lorentzian Regge configuration space, can they occupy unbounded length domains, and what additional gluing and causality conditions distinguish admissible histories?

Which positivity conditions distinguish a gravitational path integral defining universe-state inner products from one computing genuine statistical averages of boundary observables or boundary inner products?

Can the growth of the number of spacetime topologies explain a small cosmological constant through a thermodynamic interpretation of the Euclidean gravitational path integral, with added excitation producing topology rather than increasing |Λ|?

Can causality restrictions make a two-dimensional gravitational sum over spacetime topologies well defined, and what continuum dynamics, cosmological potential and wormhole density result?
